{{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|dtp|Nagasaki Kunchi|es|Nagasaki Kunchi|fa|ناگاساکی کونچی|fr|Nagasaki kunchi|id|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|ru|Нагасаки Кунти|qid=Q114712|lt=Nagasaki Kunchi}}, originally celebrated located in the northern part of the city, on the slopes of Mount Tamazono, and features a 277-step stone staircase leading up the mountain to the various buildings that comprise the shrine.

Suwa Shrine was established as a way of stopping and reverting the {{ill|Christianization|ar|تنصير|az|Xristianlaşma|bg|Християнизация|br|Kristenidigezh|ca|Cristianització|cs|Christianizace|de|Christianisierung|el|Εκχριστιανισμός|eo|Kristanigo|es|Cristianización|eu|Kristautze|fa|مسیحی‌سازی|fr|Christianisation|fy|Kerstenjen|gl|Cristianización|hr|Pokrštavanje|id|Kristenisasi|it|Cristianizzazione|ko|기독교화|lv|Kristianizācija|mk|Христијанизација|ms|Pengkristianan|nl|Kerstening|nn|Kristning|pl|Chrystianizacja|pt|Cristianização|qu|Kristiyanuchay|ro|Creștinare|ru|Христианизация|sh|Pokrštavanje|simple|Christianization|sk|Christianizácia (šírenie kresťanstva)|sr|Христијанизација|stq|Kristianisierenge|sv|Kristianisering|tl|Kristiyanisasyon|tr|Hristiyanlaşma|uk|Християнізація|zh|基督教化|zh_yue|基督教化|qid=Q59532|lt=conversion to Christianity}} that was taking place in Nagasaki.{{Cn|date=September 2023}} In modern times it remains an important and successful center of the community.

The shrine in Nagasaki is one of many Suwa shrines, all of which are dedicated to Suwa-no-Kami, a {{ill|Kami|abstract|Q524158|ar|كامي|ary|كامي|as|কামি|az|Kami|azb|کامی|bcl|Kami|bg|Ками|bn|কামি|ca|Kami|cs|Kami|da|Kami|de|Kami|el|Κάμι (Σιντοϊσμός)|eo|Kamio|es|Kami|et|Kami|eu|Kami|fa|کامی|fi|Kami|fr|Kami (divinité)|gd|Kami (dia)|he|קאמי (שינטו)|hi|कामी|hr|Kami|hu|Kami|hy|Կամի|id|Kami (mitologi)|it|Kami|ja|神 (神道)|ka|კამი|ko|카미|lb|Kami|lfn|Cami|lt|Kami|mk|Ками|ml|കാമി|mni|ꯀꯃꯤ|mr|कामी|ms|Kami (Shinto)|nl|Kami (god)|no|Kami|or|କାମି|pl|Kami (mitologia japońska)|pt|Kami|ro|Kami|rsk|Ками|ru|Ками|sc|Kami|simple|Kami|sl|Kami|sq|Kami|sr|Ками (јапанско божанство)|sv|Kami|ta|காமி|te|కామి|tok|kon Kami|tr|Kami (Şintoizm)|uk|Камі|ur|کامی|vi|Kami|zh|神 (神道)|zh_yue|神 (神道)|qid=Q524158|lt=kami}} of valor and duty, and are linked with {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa taisha}}, the head shrine of Suwa-no-Kami worship. Two other kami are also enshrined at Suwa Shrine, all three of which are celebrated during Kunchi.

The government had begun forcing Christians to reconvert to the Japanese religions of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|de|Shinbutsu-Shūgō|es|Shinbutsu shūgō|eu|Shinbutsu-shūgō|fa|شینبوتسو-شوگو|fi|Shinbutsu shūgō|fr|Shinbutsu shūgō|id|Shinbutsu-shūgō|it|Shinbutsu shūgō|ja|神仏習合|ko|신불습합|pl|Synkretyzm shintō-buddyjski|ru|Синто-буддийский синкретизм|th|ชิมบุตสึชูโง|tr|Şinbutsu-şuugō|uk|Синто-буддистський синкретизм|ur|شنتو اور بدھ مت کا امتزاج ضدین|zh|神佛習合|qid=Q2279088|lt=shinbutsu-shūgō}}. It was thought that establishing a major point of Shinto worship would be important to these efforts, giving the local population a central point of worship and a sense of community.<ref name="Nelson">Nelson, John K., ''A Year in the Life of a Shinto Shrine, USA, University of Washington Press, 1996, {{ISBN|0-295-97500-8}}</ref>

In 1623, Aoki Kensei (1582-1656), a [[Shugendō]] priest, came to Nagasaki.<ref name=":0" /> With the backing of the {{ill|Shogun|af|Sjogoen|ar|شوغون|az|Şoqun|bcl|Shōgun|be|Сёгун|bg|Шогун|bn|শোগুন|br|Shogun|ca|Shogun|ckb|شۆگن|cs|Šógun|cv|Сёгун|da|Shogun|de|Shōgun|el|Σόγκουν|eo|Ŝoguno|es|Shōgun|et|Šogun|eu|Shogun|fa|شوگون|fi|Shōgun|fr|Shogun|frr|Schoguun|gl|Shōgun|hak|Chṳ̂n-yì Thai-chiông-kiûn|he|שוגון|hi|शोगुन|hr|Šogun|hu|Sógun|hy|Սյոգուն|id|Shōgun|is|Sjógun|it|Shōgun|ja|征夷大将軍|jv|Shogun|ka|სიოგუნი|kk|Сегунат|ko|쇼군|krc|Сёгун|la|Xogun|lt|Šiogūnas|lv|Sjoguns|min|Syogun|mk|Шогун|ml|ഷോഗൺ|mn|Шогун|mr|शोगुन|ms|Shōgun|my|ရှိုးဂန်း|nl|Shogun (titel)|nn|Shogun|no|Shogun|pa|ਸ਼ੋਗੁਨ|pl|Siogun|pnb|شوگون|pt|Xogum|ro|Shogun|ru|Сёгун|sc|Shōgun|sco|Shōgun|sh|Šogun|simple|Shōgun|sk|Šógun|sl|Šogun|sq|Shoguni|sr|Шогун|su|Sogun|sv|Shogun|ta|ஷோகன்|th|โชกุน|tl|Shogun|tr|Şogun|tt|Sögun|ug|شوگۇن|uk|Сьоґун|ur|شوگون|vi|Shōgun|war|Shogun|wuu|征夷大将军|xmf|შოგუნი|zh|征夷大將軍|zh_classical|征夷大將軍|zh_min_nan|Cheng-î Tāi-chiong-kun|zh_yue|幕府將軍|qid=Q131767|lt=Shogun}} and the Nagasaki's magistrate, land on His religious zeal and skill at organizing, combined with authority granted by the leading Yoshida Shinto council, led to the Completion of the main structure of Suwa Shrine in 1626.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Nelson"/> In order to attract attention and encourage attendance at the new shrine, a dramatic ''yutate-sai'' ritual, where a priest demonstrates his communion with the kami by plunging his hands into boiling water unharmed, was performed. In spite of this, as well as the {{ill|Sumo|ar|سومو|ast|Sumo|az|Sumo|ba|Сумо|bcl|Sumo wrestling|be|Сумо|bg|Сумо|bn|সুমো|bo|སུ་མོ་སྦེ་ག|br|Sumo|bs|Sumo hrvanje|ca|Sumo|cs|Sumó|da|Sumo|de|Sumō|el|Σούμο|eo|Sumoo|es|Sumo|et|Sumo|eu|Sumo|fa|سومو|fi|Sumo|fo|Sumo-glíming|fr|Sumo|frp|Sumo|fy|Sûmo|ga|Súmó|gd|Sumo|gl|Sumo|gor|Sumo|he|סומו|hi|सूमो|hr|Sumo hrvanje|hu|Szumó|hy|Սումո|hyw|Սումօ (մարտարուեստ)|ia|Sumo|id|Sumo|io|Sumo (luktado)|it|Sumo|ja|相撲|jv|Sumo|ka|სუმო|kk|Сумо|km|ស៊ូម៉ូ|kn|ಸುಮೋ|ko|스모|ky|Сумо|la|Sumo (colluctatio)|lt|Sumo|lv|Sumo|mk|Сумо|ml|സുമോ ഗുസ്തി|mn|Сүмо|mr|सुमो|ms|Sumo|my|ဆူမို|ne|सुमो|new|सुमो|nl|Sumo|nn|Sumobryting|no|Sumo|nov|Sumo|oc|Sumo|os|Сумо|pl|Sumo|pms|Sumo|pt|Sumô|ro|Sumo|ru|Сумо|sc|Sumo|scn|Sumo|sh|Sumo|simple|Sumo|sk|Sumo|sq|Sumo|sr|Сумо|sv|Sumo|sw|Sumo|ta|சுமோ மற்போர்|te|సుమో యోధులు|th|ซูโม่|tr|Sumo|ug|سۇمو|uk|Сумо|uz|Sumo|vi|Sumo|wa|Sumô|war|Sumo|wuu|相扑|xmf|სუმო|zh|相撲|zh_min_nan|Siong-phok|zh_yue|相撲|zu|Sumo|qid=Q40561|lt=sumo match}} that followed, very few people came to watch.<ref name="Nelson"/>

In 1634, an edict was issued requiring all people to register at the shrine and be counted.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Smyers |first=Karen A. |date=1996 |title=Review of A Year in the Life of a Shinto Shrine |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2385441 |journal=Monumenta Nipponica |volume=51 |issue=4 |pages=513–515 |doi=10.2307/2385441 |issn=0027-0741}}</ref> In addition to this, in another attempt to further increase local participation in shrine events, a great autumn festival was held at the shrine. Both of these events were created in the attempt to discover any remaining Christians, who would not be able to participate in the festival or register at the shrine. Anyone who failed to do so was arrested, tortured and possibly executed if they did not renounce their Christian faith.<ref name="Nelson"/>

Suwa Shrine was relocated further up the slope of the mountain twice, first in 1647 and then again in 1683.<ref name=":0" />

These performances continued until 1856, when a major fire at the shrine destroyed most of the expensive Noh masks and props.

From 1871 through 1946, Suwa was officially designated one of the {{nihongo|''[[:en:Kokuhei-chūsha|Kokuhei-chūsha]]''|国幣中社}}, meaning that it stood in the mid-range of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked, nationally significant shrines]].

August 9, 1945.  It is thought to have survived intact due to its strategic location in the central part of Mount Tamazono's southern flank, although in the aftermath of the bomb local residents were quick to note that while the famous [[:en:Urakami Cathedral|Urakami Cathedral]] and surrounding Catholic neighborhoods were obliterated, the Shinto shrine still stood.

This was considered to be significant by the survivors of the bombing, showing the power of the native Japanese kami as opposed to the imported {{ill|God the Father|ar|الله الآب|arc|ܐܒܐ (ܐܠܗܐ)|arz|الله الاب|ast|Dios Padre|az|Xristianlıqda Ata|be|Бог Айцец|bg|Бог Отец|bn|পিতা ঈশ্বর|br|Doue an Tad|ca|Déu Pare|ckb|خودای باوک|co|Patre|cs|Bůh Otec|cv|Турă Атте|da|Gud Fader|de|Gott der Vater|eo|Dio Patro|es|Dios Padre|eu|Jainko Aita|fa|خدای پدر|fr|Dieu le Père|gl|Deus Pai|he|האל האב|hi|परमपिता परमेश्वर|hr|Bog Otac|hy|Հայր Աստված|id|Allah Bapa|it|Dio Padre|ja|父なる神|ka|მამა ღმერთი|ko|성부|la|Deus Pater|lt|Dievas Tėvas|mg|Andriamanitra Ray|mk|Господ-Отецот|ml|പിതാവായ ദൈവം|ms|Tuhan Bapa|mt|Alla l-Missier|nl|God de Vader|nn|Gud Fader|no|Gud Fader|pl|Bóg Ojciec|pnb|خدا باپ|pt|Deus, o Pai|ro|Dumnezeu Tatăl|ru|Бог Отец|scn|Patraternu|sh|Bog Otac|simple|God the Father|sk|Boh Otec|sr|Бог Отац|sv|Fadern|sw|Mungu Baba|szl|Bůg Uojćec|ta|தந்தையாம் கடவுள்|th|พระเจ้าพระบิดา|tl|Diyos Ama|tr|Baba (Hristiyanlık)|uk|Бог Отець|ur|خدا باپ|vi|Chúa Cha|wuu|圣父|xmf|მუმა ღორონთი|zh|聖父|zh_yue|聖父|qid=Q186350|lt=Christian god}}. In addition, priests from Suwa Shrine took an active role in the rebuilding of Nagasaki, including consecrating the land and purifying structures that still stood.<ref name="Nelson" />

In 1984, a large-scale reconstruction repaired and modernized the shrine, installing such conveniences as {{ill|Air conditioner|ar|مكيف الهواء|az|Kondisioner|be|Кандыцыянер|da|Klimaanlæg|es|Acondicionador autónomo|fr|Climatiseur|hr|Klimatizacijski uređaj|hu|Légkondicionáló|hy|Օդորակիչ|it|Condizionatore d'aria|ja|エア・コンディショナー|ka|კონდიციონერი|kk|Кондиционер|ko|에어컨|la|Instrumentum aëri temperando|lv|Kondicionieris|pl|Klimatyzator|ru|Кондиционер|simple|Air conditioner|so|Mashinka Dabaylka|sr|Klima uređaj|ta|காற்றுச்சீரமைப்பி|tr|Klima|uk|Кондиціонер|uz|Konditsioner|vi|Máy điều hòa không khí|yi|לופטקילער|zh_yue|冷氣機|qid=Q1265533|lt=Air conditioner}}s and glass windows. This reconstruction was controversial, as some felt that modern conveniences had no place at a traditional shrine.

==Festivals==

'' at the shrine]]
Like most Shinto shrines, every year thousands of people visit Suwa Shrine to pray for peace and prosperity. The Shrine is also the main destination in Nagasaki for events such as [[Shichi-Go-San]] and {{ill|Coming of Age Day|cs|Seidžin no hi|de|Seijin no Hi|es|Seijin no Hi|eu|Seijin no Hi|fa|روز ورود به بزرگسالی|he|יום ההתבגרות|hu|A felnőtté válás napja|id|Hari Kedewasaan|it|Seijin no hi|ja|成人の日|ko|성인의 날|ms|Hari Orang Dewasa|my|အရွယ်ရောက်သူများနေ့|ru|День совершеннолетия|ta|வயதுவந்த நாள்|th|วันบรรลุนิติภาวะ|tr|Yetişkinler Günü|uk|День повноліття|vi|Ngày Thành Nhân|zh|成人之日|qid=Q483226|lt=the coming-of-age day}} ceremonies.

Suwa Shrine is also the host to many annual festivals. These festivals serve the joint purpose of honoring the kami, providing a sense of community for shrine worshipers, and providing exposure and income for the shrine itself. Some of these festivals are typical to all major Shinto shrines in Japan, but some are unique to Suwa Shrine.

* '''Atomic bomb commemorative service''' - This festival is probably unique in all of Japan, in that it combines elements of Christian, Buddhist and Shinto worship to pray for the 35,000-40,000 people killed by the atomic bomb dropped on Nagasaki. It takes place every year on August 9.
* '''Doll's Festival''' - Like all of Japan, Suwa Shrine observes the [[:en:Hina Matsuri|Doll's Festival]] on March 3. However, since the 1980s the festival has been observed in an unusual way, in that attractive, 20-year-old women are selected to wear the shrine's collection of antique {{ill|Kimono|af|Kimono|ar|كيمون (لباس)|ary|كيمونو|az|Kimono|bcl|Kimono|be|Кімано|bg|Кимоно|bn|কিমোনো|ca|Quimono|cs|Kimono|da|Kimono|de|Kimono|eo|Kimono|es|Kimono|eu|Kimono|fa|کیمونو|fi|Kimono|fr|Kimono|gan|和服|gl|Quimono|gn|Kimóno|gor|Kimono|he|קימונו|hr|Kimono|ht|Kimono|hu|Kimonó|hy|Կիմոնո|ia|Kimono|id|Kimono|io|Kimono|is|Kimono|it|Kimono|ja|和服|jv|Kimono|ka|კიმონო|kk|Кимоно|km|គីម៉ូណូ|ko|기모노|ks|کیمونو|lt|Kimono|lv|Kimono|mk|Кимоно|ml|കിമോണോ|mn|Кимоно|ms|Kimono|my|ကီမိုနို|ne|किमोनो|nl|Kimono|nn|Kimono|no|Kimono|or|କିମୋନୋ|pl|Kimono|pnb|کمونو|pt|Quimono|ro|Kimono|ru|Кимоно|sa|किमोनो|scn|Chimonu|sh|Kimono|simple|Kimono|sk|Kimono|sl|Kimono|sq|Kimono|sr|Кимоно|su|Kimono|sv|Kimono|ta|கிமோனோ|th|กิโมโน|tl|Kimono|tr|Kimono|ug|كىمونو|uk|Кімоно|ur|کیمونو|uz|Kimono|vi|Kimono|war|Kimono|wuu|和服|zh|和服|zh_classical|和服|zh_min_nan|Hô-ho̍k|zh_yue|和服|qid=Q483444|lt=Kimono}} and pose in a live Doll's Day procession. The competition among the young women is fierce, and there are far more applicants than positions in the festival.  The two most beautiful women are chosen for the key roles of the Emperor and Empress in the procession. This tradition was created largely as a {{ill|Media event|ar|حدث إعلامي|de|Medienereignis|es|Suceso mediático|he|אירוע מדיה|id|Peristiwa media|no|Mediebegivenhet|pt|Evento midiático|ru|Псевдособытие|tr|Medya etkinliği|vi|Sự kiện truyền thông|zh|媒体事件|qid=Q1457237|lt=Media event}} to promote and advertise Suwa Shrine, and every year television crews are invited to broadcast the festival.<ref name="Nelson"/>

* '''Kunchi''' - The most famous of Suwa Shrine's festivals, this festival began along with the founding of the shrine as a way to both demonstrate its new importance in the community and as a way to hunt for {{ill|Kakure Kirishitan|ar|الكاكوري كيريشتيان|be_x_old|Какурэ кірысітан|cs|Kakure kirišitan|fa|مسیحیان پنهان|fi|Kakure kirishitan|fr|Kakure kirishitan|he|קקורה קירישיטן|id|Kakure Kirishitan|it|Kakure kirishitan|ja|隠れキリシタン|ko|가쿠레키리시탄|la|Kakure Kirishitan|ms|Kakure Kirishitan|no|Kakure kirishitan|pl|Kakure-kirishitan|pt|Kakure Kirishitan|ru|Какурэ-кириситан|sr|Скривени хришћани|sv|Kakure kirishitan|th|คากูเระคิริชิตัง|tr|Kakure Kirishitan|uk|Підпільні християни|vi|Kakure Kirishitan|zh|隱匿基督徒|qid=Q1524983|lt=Hidden Christians}}. Kunchi is held from October 7 to 9 every year and is considered one of the major festivals of Osaka's Tenjin Matsuri.{{Disputed inline|date=September 2023}} It has been designated as an Important Intangible Cultural Asset.<ref name="Nelson"/>
* '''Yutate-sai''' - A theatrical ritual, originally performed by [[yamabushi]], a priest demonstrates his communion with the kami by plunging his hands into boiling water unharmed. This ritual was performed on the opening of Suwa Shrine, and is continued to be performed to this day. It is very rare at other Shinto shrines.{{Cn|date=September 2023}}

==English language fortunes==

Most Shinto shrines sell {{ill|O-mikuji|ar|او ميكوجي|ca|Omikuji|cs|Omikudži|da|Omikuji|de|Omikuji|el|Ομίκουζι|es|Omikuji|et|Omikuji|fr|Omikuji|id|Omikuji|it|Omikuji|ja|おみくじ|ko|오미쿠지|ms|Omikuji|my|အိုမိခုဂျိ|pl|O-mikuji|pt|Omikuji|ru|Омикудзи|th|โอมิกูจิ|tr|Omikuji|vi|O-mikuji|zh|御神籤|qid=Q1069592|lt=omikuji}}, a type of fortune telling that comes on a slip of paper that lists your particular luck at that time. Suwa Shrine was the first shrine in Japan to offer omikuji in English.{{Cn|date=September 2023}}

==Stop lions==

Another unique feature of Suwa Shrine are the "stop lions". They are two stone-carved {{ill|Komainu|ar|كوماينو|as|কোমাইনু|de|Komainu|et|Komainu|fa|کومااینو|fr|Komainu|hu|Komainu|ja|狛犬|ko|코마이누|pl|Komainu|pt|Komainu|ru|Комаину|simple|Komainu|sq|Komainu|zh|狛犬|qid=Q20155846|lt=guardian lions}}, and tradition holds that if one wishes to stop a behavior, such as {{ill|Smoking cessation|af|Rookstaking|ar|إقلاع عن التدخين|ban|Puput ngroko|ca|Cessació tabàquica|cs|Odvykání kouření|es|Cesación tabáquica|fa|ترک سیگار|fi|Tupakoinnin lopettaminen|fr|Sevrage tabagique|ha|Daina shan taba|he|גמילה מעישון|hy|Նիկոտինային կախվածությունից բուժում|id|Penghentian merokok|ka|ნიკოტინომანია|nl|Stoppen met roken|no|Røykeslutt|pt|Cessação tabágica|ro|Renunțarea la fumat|ru|Лечение никотиновой зависимости|sl|Opustitev kajenja|sq|Ndërprerja e duhanit|sv|Rökavvänjning|sw|Kuacha kuvuta sigara|uk|Лікування нікотинової залежності|vi|Cai thuốc lá|zh|戒烟|zh_yue|戒煙|qid=Q2462253|lt=smoking}}, one should tie a piece of paper or string around their front legs and pray for their assistance.
